Arbiter accept/event 3.0-3.15 ~ native 3.076 = sub-deployment-impact.

re.onlineFindings: Lossless-specdec literature (emergentmind) states the academically correct frame: 'every emitted token is the target model's greedy argmax at verification time, though output can still differ from pure autoregressive because of NUMERICAL DISPATCH DIVERGENCE.' This is precisely FR13: the 21 flips are tree-verify (one dispatch) vs no-spec DECODE (the autoregressive oracle, a different dispatch) — so the binding gate should be cat9-tree-verify vs native-MTP-tree-verify (same dispatch class), NOT vs the no-spec decode oracle; part of the 21 is the EXPECTED dispatch gap, not a bug (flagged in FR13_BV_GEOMETRY 'NEXT', never re-measured). STree (arXiv 2505.14969, the GDN-hybrid tree-decode reference): tree decoding on SSMs requires ACCUMULATING state-transition matrices per the tree; the recurrent state replay is the bf16-sensitive path — corroborates the durable-state handoff (replay route) as the hard part for GDN/Mamba hybrids, not the per-forward scan. Component-aware self-spec in hybrids (2605.01106) + SpecMamba (2509.19873): bf16 recurrent-state replay AND small projections are the numerically fragile paths needing stabilization across speculative cycles — confirms BOTH projection (in_proj_ba/qkv_proj) AND recurrent replay are right targets and MORE THAN ONE needs stabilizing. Sources: arxiv.org/abs/2505.14969, emergentmind.com/topics/lossless-speculative-decoding, arxiv.org/html/2605.01106, arxiv.org/pdf/2509.19873, openreview.net/pdf?id=r8H7xhYPwz.
